title: Sorting and grouping: change presentation while preserving requests
goal: Order requests by duration, group them by customer and distinguish presentation from data edits and report totals.

prerequisites.text: 1c-enterprise.a 2; A1–A2: separate infobase, catalogs, references and documents; synthetic data only.

sections.title: Sorting changes row order
paragraphs: Clicking the numeric column header changes list order; another click switches direction. Check actual values rather than guessing a small arrow’s meaning. For 30, 45, 30 and 15, ascending order is 15, 30, 30, 45; descending is 45, 30, 30, 15.

Document numbers and fields do not change. The second row after sorting may be a different request. Identify your document by its actual number. Equal durations do not guarantee a particular relative order without an additional sort criterion.

sections.title: One dataset, several presentations
paragraphs: Two documents can share duration 30 without being duplicates.

code.source:
First customer: 30, 45, 30. Second: 15.
Ascending: 15, 30, 30, 45.
Descending: 45, 30, 30, 15.
By customer: three documents and one.
code.output: Order and headings change while four numbers and values are preserved.

sections.title: Grouping puts related details under a heading
paragraphs: Grouping by Клиент places requests linked to the same customer under one heading. This uses a customer reference rather than similar text. Two same-named customer records can form different groups; investigate identity before changing names for cosmetic consistency.
A plus beside a group expands its details. A collapsed group does not imply missing or deleted documents. Its heading is not an additional request: count document numbers rather than visible bands.

sections.title: Keep one dataset for subsequent lessons
paragraphs: The sequential route already has 30, 45 and 30 minutes for the first customer, including the corrected request from the preceding lesson. Add one separate 15-minute request for the existing second customer Учебный Юг, using the existing service. Preserve earlier records.

If you already created that request, reuse its number instead of duplicating it. The basic example has three first-customer requests and one second-customer request. Preserve additional work and recalculate expected groups from your actual table.

sections.title: A collapsed group still retains data
paragraphs: Expanding a group shows a detail; it does not create a document.

code.source: Click the second customer’s plus sign and inspect its 15-minute detail.
code.output: The same saved request and number become visible.

sections.title: Order, group and aggregate are different
paragraphs: Sorting chooses order, grouping organizes related details and filtering chooses which rows are included. They can act together. Disable your duration filter before sorting, otherwise excluded values remain hidden. Grouped presentation can also affect where a sort is applied.

A normal list grouping does not promise an automatic duration total in the heading. The next lesson’s separate report calculates count and minutes as aggregates. Here reconcile numbers and manually calculate 105 minutes for the first customer and 15 for the second.

sections.title: Check your explanation
paragraphs: Sorting changes which document appears in the second row. Identify your request by actual number rather than its former position.
A collapsed heading hides details without deleting documents. Expand the plus sign and reconcile numbers with your baseline.
Normal list grouping is not itself a report with duration aggregates. Calculate totals manually, then compare them with the separate report in the next lesson.

selfcheck.feedback: An equal field value does not establish one record.

selfcheck.prompt: Distinguish filtering, sorting, grouping and aggregation; prepare an independent table for the report.
selfcheck.feedback: Basic totals: first customer three/105, second one/15; additional work accounted for.

practice.title: Explore request order and customer groups
practice.task: Distinguish filtering, sorting, grouping and aggregation; prepare an independent table for the report.
practice.environment: Official training 1C, the same own infobase and existing catalog items; no Studio, code or CF reload required.
practice.externalRoute: Installed Enterprise mode → Заявка услуги list

steps.title: Prepare a fourth request without duplication
steps.action: Locate the existing second customer Учебный Юг. If no 15-minute training request for this exercise exists, create one with the existing service and Новая, save and record its number. Otherwise reuse it. Record all your numbers and durations.
steps.why: Use multiple first-customer requests and one second-customer request while preserving earlier work.
steps.expected: The basic sequence has 30, 45, 30 for the first customer and 15 for the second.
steps.troubleshooting: Preserve additional records and include them in your own table rather than deleting them to match a picture.
steps.before: Earlier requests and their numbers remain in your own infobase. Search is clear and your numeric filter is disabled.

steps.title: Check list restrictions
steps.action: Clear search, disable ≥45 and your other filters, and ensure the period includes all prepared request dates.
steps.why: Sorting does not restore rows excluded by an active filter.
steps.troubleshooting: Check restrictions before entering a missing request again.
steps.before: The basic sequence has 30, 45, 30 for the first customer and 15 for the second.

steps.title: Sort by increasing duration
steps.action: Click the header; if actual values decrease, click again. Compare with your predicted order and identify both 30-minute request numbers.
steps.why: Read direction from values and distinguish position from identity.
steps.expected: The basic values are 15, 30, 30, 45; both 30-minute documents remain.
steps.troubleshooting: Do not demand a fixed order among equal values without a second criterion.

figures.caption: Sorting the separate 30/45/15 test yields 15/30/45. Preserve both 30-minute requests in your own course sequence.
figures.alt: Sorting the separate 30/45/15 test yields 15/30/45. Preserve both 30-minute requests in your own course sequence.

steps.title: Reverse the direction
steps.action: Click again and compare the reversed order without editing any duration.
steps.why: A reversible order change must preserve contents.
steps.troubleshooting: Click the heading rather than selecting a document cell.
steps.before: The basic values are 15, 30, 30, 45; both 30-minute documents remain.

figures.caption: Reversing gives 45/30/15 for the same three test documents without changing their values.
figures.alt: Reversing gives 45/30/15 for the same three test documents without changing their values.

steps.title: Group by customer
steps.action: Open Группировка and double-click Клиент on the left. Verify the enabled Клиент field on the right and choose Завершить редактирование.
steps.why: Select existing customer references as the grouping key.
steps.expected: Customer headings appear with groups of three and one in the basic dataset.
steps.troubleshooting: Do not substitute a name field without understanding identity. Expand collapsed details with the plus sign.

figures.caption: The Группировка tab enables Клиент: a catalog reference, not arbitrary similar text.
figures.alt: The Группировка tab enables Клиент: a catalog reference, not arbitrary similar text.

steps.title: Expand and reconcile details
steps.action: Expand both groups, compare every number and duration and manually total 30+45+30=105 and 15 separately. Optionally disable Клиент in grouping settings to restore a flat list.
steps.why: Details remain stored; manual totals provide independent expectations for the report.
steps.expected: All four numbers are available; grouping created or deleted no documents.
steps.troubleshooting: Do not count headings as documents. Include additional requests in your actual totals.
steps.before: Customer headings appear with groups of three and one in the basic dataset.

figures.caption: The second customer’s 15-minute detail is expanded. Group headings are not additional requests; this test baseline has three documents.
figures.alt: The second customer’s 15-minute detail is expanded. Group headings are not additional requests; this test baseline has three documents.

criteria: Four separate numbers identified; equal field values are not deleted as duplicates.
Presentation changes reversibly and original documents remain intact.
Basic totals: first customer three/105, second one/15; additional work accounted for.
Numbers, durations and customers before and after presentation changes.
Both directions, expanded groups and independent synthetic totals.
Do not delete equal durations as duplicates or mistake a collapsed group for lost data.
